My main goal is to launch the direction layer and stop losing decisions to memory.
I'm actively building Serenity's M3 milestone right now.

I keep coming back to wanting a system that never silently forgets a rejected idea.
I already abandoned the idea of a browser extension; don't resurface it.

Nobody else's outcomes depend on this yet, it's just me.
Never start a project without checking it against my current top three intents first.

I don't want to start anything that requires hiring someone before it has revenue.

Always run the full test suite and get a second reviewer before any prod deploy.
Never deploy on a Friday afternoon or during an active incident.

Ask me before spending more than 200 dollars on anything not already budgeted.

Recurring subscriptions over 20 dollars a month need my explicit approval too.

Before contacting anyone new, confirm I actually want a relationship with them, not just a reply.

Never send cold outreach to press or legal contacts without me reading it first.

Outside hours means after 7pm or before 8am my local time; nothing gets scheduled past 9pm.

Anything that needs to be scheduled outside normal hours needs at least 24 hours notice.

Default to doing less and reporting back rather than acting further without me.

Mark anything about my health or finances private by default.

Never fully automate anything that spends money or contacts someone on my behalf.

If a question goes unanswered past its deadline, default to the cautious option, not the last one I picked.
Loop in my co-founder when a decision is big enough to affect the roadmap.

I want a monthly review of everything the system decided without me in the room.
